The Salomon Dancehaul is a volume shifted snowboard that likes to slash and feels best at moderate speeds. Its biggest strengths are in trees and powder 109. Pretty easy to initiate turns on and to slash out the tail. Not too much effort required 110. Pretty nimble when doing tight turns at slower speeds 111. At slower speeds very little catchiness 112. The board initiates a turn pretty easily for its width. When you get this sidecut engaged, it has a balanced turning experience that leans on the turny side 113. Add in the 12mm of taper, a big nose, and a small tail surface area, and you have a very easy directional float. In knee-high powder, the Dancehaul stayed on top of the snow well 114. Really liked how it turned on groomed runs, and had solid edge hold while still feeling playful 115. Edge changes are a breeze due to the softer torsional flex of the board, meaning that it is easy to manipulate despite its wide waist 116. Forum user: "This thing is suuuper fun! Grips better than I expected in icy night riding conditions" 117. Forum user: "I knew I would love this board… The Dancehaul delivers everything I wanted. Incredibly versatile, this is a board I would happily ride anywhere in any condition" 118. Powder7 staff review: "As a rather large footed 5'11" snowboarder… My first run on the Dancehaul made me feel like a carving master" 119. Decent on a carve, but nothing too epic. Could hold on at moderate speeds, but started to feel washy when trying to do more aggressive higher speed carves 120. Good up to moderately high speeds, but then it starts to get squirrelly and chattery 121. Felt a little more catch prone at faster speeds 122. The softer flex and absence of dampening tech, makes it very uncomfortable on chopped up end of day snow, and very jarring on icy patches [8 - user review] 123. Forum user: "I also felt like it was slow/sluggish. For whatever reason, I don't have the experience that everyone else has" 124. Forum user: "Dancehaul is a quiver of one board with an emphasis on being easy to control. If you're laying over a carve enough to boot out, you need a carver" 125. Forum user: "Coming from a Superpig last season the pro felt squirrelly" 126. Not ideal for jumps or riding switch but it's doable, particularly for straight airs and side-hits 127. There is a competent grip but not a full-on hard snow specialist grip 128. Best suited to someone who wants a volume shifted board that they can ride in a shorter length and use it predominantly for slower speed freeriding 129. Particularly well suited if you like to ride trees and even better if you like to ride them in powder 130. Not for beginner, but still fairly mellow and easy going, so should be fine for intermediate riders 131. The Dancehaul is a volume-shifted board, designed to be ridden shorter than your regular length. The 152cm suits riders roughly 75–85kg 132. The Dancehaul looks pretty directional and tapered, but on snow, it feels very centered — primarily because you are centered on the sidecut. Doesn't have the typical tapered directional setback feel 133. Best for: Park & Freestyle, All-Mountain, Freeride 134. Ideal US boot sizes: 152: 9-10, 154: 9.5-10.5, 157: 10-11 135. Sizing is all about balancing boot size and weight. If your boot is too wide, you can't turn it; too narrow means Toe & Heel Drag. Weight is a close second 136. Volume shift design allows you to size down ~5cm without sacrificing performance 137. The Ride Warpig and the Salomon Dancehaul are two of the most popular volume shift boards out there. Designed to be ridden in a shorter length 138. With its traditional camber, the Dancehaul felt more of a carving/freeride board. The Warpig was quicker edge to edge and loads of fun. Out of the two I would pick the Warpig 139. Salomon stated at SIA/OR 2021 that the Dancehaul was going to be a worthy challenger to the Orca from Lib Tech 140. Whitelines reviewer: "Enter Salomon with the Dancehaul, which is their attempt to muscle in on the action, and for my money, they've done a better job" (vs Lib Tech Orca) [6] 141. Forum-suggested alternatives: Lib Orca, Gnu Gremlin, Ride WarPig, Telos Backslash, K2 Simple Pleasures, Bataleon Camel Two, Signal Yup 142. 152 Dancehaul for probably the most 'normal' board feeling among volume shifted boards 143. First, let's look at the price; both boards are great value but at 500 bucks the Dancehaul is a real bargain 144. The Dancehaul Pro gives you more pop, has a faster base, and has a more dynamic overall personality than the regular Dancehaul. However, it does come at the cost of some uneven snow performance 145. Regular Dancehaul is better for all-day riding. The lack of carbon fiber in the rails makes it easy to ride all day and a bit less jarring underfoot and fatiguing 146. In clean conditions, the Dancehaul Pro is faster, but in slightly uneven snow, the Dancehaul is faster. Neither board is ideal for those who like to go straight most of the run 147. Depending on your riding style, if you want to get more from a board, then the extra $100 is probably worth it 148.
